A Mandelbrot and Julia explorer in two halves that share no code: a Go core
for headless image generation and export, and a native SwiftUI app for interactive
exploration. Neither imports the other.

Go half:
  - Module github.com/AnthonyWest/fractals-from-the-90s, Go 1.26, ~7,800
    lines.
  - internal/ holds thirteen single-responsibility packages. Each owns one
    concern and is imported by name. There is no registry, plugin mechanism
    or dependency-injection layer, so the relationships between packages are
    ordinary Go imports and nothing else.
  - cmd/ holds two command binaries, each a main package in its own
    directory.
  - Tests are conventional _test.go files beside the code they cover, thirty
    of them across internal/ and cmd/.
  - testdata/golden/ holds recorded output the export tests compare against.

Swift half:
  - apple/FractalApp/ is an Xcode project. Sources live in
    apple/FractalApp/FractalApp/, unit tests in
    apple/FractalApp/FractalAppTests/.
  - The convention is one main type per file, named after the type, though
    several files declare a few closely related types alongside it.
  - apple/FractalApp/build/ and any DerivedData directory are build output,
    not source. Nothing under them should be read or cited.

Supporting, not part of either build:
  - docs/ carries architecture notes, ADRs and design records.
  - scripts/ is repo hygiene and git hooks; tools/ holds one Python analysis
    helper. --disallowedTools Agent,Task,WebSearch,WebFetch
